core_obligations: Construct the map c -> c cap [S]_1 from bivariant classes to CH_{1-p}(X) (proof lines 14743-14748).

For alpha in CH_{1-p}(X), define c_alpha by c_alpha cap alpha' = alpha times alpha' and prove it is bivariant by decomposing alpha into integral components and handling the dominating and non-dominating cases separately (proof lines 14750-14784).
Show the two constructions are mutually inverse, reducing the second direction to an integral test scheme X' and to the two cases of the structure morphism X' -> S (proof lines 14786-14804).
proof_roadmap: Construction and bivariance of c_alpha (proof lines 14750-14784).
Second inverse identity via the two cases for X' (proof lines 14786-14804).
difficulty_reason: For a base (S, delta) of dimension one and a scheme X locally of finite type over S, the lemma asserts a canonical identification A^p(X -> S) = CH_{1-p}(X) for all integers p (statement lines 14733-14741). The proof constructs both directions: sending a bivariant class c to c cap [S]_1 gives a map A^p(X -> S) -> CH_{1-p}(X), and conversely an element alpha of CH_{1-p}(X) defines c_alpha by c_alpha cap alpha' = alpha times alpha' in CH_{n-p}(X x_S X') (proof lines 14743-14748 and 14780-14784). To see that c_alpha is a bivariant class the proof writes alpha = sum n_i [X_i] as in Definition labelled definition-cycles, so that g : coprod_i X_i -> X is proper, and builds the class componentwise: if X_i dominates an irreducible component of S then p_i : X_i -> S is flat and xi_i = p_i^*, while if p_i factors through a closed point s_i then xi_i = (p'_i)^* o c_i with c_i the Gysin homomorphism of s_i in S; since A^p(coprod_i X_i -> S) is the product of the A^p(X_i -> S), the sum xi = sum n_i xi_i makes sense and g_* o xi is bivariant by Lemma labelled lemma-push-proper-bivariant, and the proof states that the reader easily verifies that c_alpha equals this class (proof lines 14750-14778). The two constructions are then shown to be mutually inverse: one direction is c_alpha cap [S]_1 = alpha, and for the other, with alpha = c cap [S]_1, it suffices by Lemma labelled lemma-bivariant-zero to prove c cap [X'] = c_alpha cap [X'] for integral X' locally of finite type over S, where either p' : X' -> S is flat of relative dimension dim_delta(X') - 1 and [X'] = (p')^*[S]_1 or X' -> S factors through a closed point and [X'] = (p')^*(s -> S)^*[S]_1, after which commutation of bivariant classes with flat pullback and Gysin maps finishes the argument (proof lines 14786-14804). Splitting the construction of the class along the two kinds of components, and then reducing the inverse identity to the two cases for an integral test scheme, is the non-formal step, so the claim is H2; the step called easy by the author is recorded verbatim in the editorial notes.
